text:
Forensic findings
1) Domain context: An institutional records office files incoming correspondence by date, subject, and sender; assigns a tracking number; indexes by category; stores originals in a filing system with an access log; and retains records per a retention schedule. Periodic audits verify that each file has an index entry, an unbroken custody chain, and retention compliance. Communications are logged with timestamps, participant identifiers, and message hashes. The intake topic is not named here, and no wrongdoing is named here.

2) What occurred: The actor initiated a multi-party coordination sequence. A dated record was created in the records office filing system, indexed under a coordination subject line. The actor linked a named account to at least three competing landlord records and opened a channel between them. In that channel, the actor transmitted messages proposing a uniform rent increase schedule, a geographic market division (neighborhood allotments), and a penalty clause for any participant who priced below the agreed level. The actor then migrated the channel to an ephemeral, self-deleting medium and instructed participants to avoid logging identifiers. The actor amended the original filing-system index entry to remove the coordination subject line and replaced it with a neutral administrative subject. The actor purged the message log for the original channel and deleted the local copies. A custody-chain audit later revealed the index entry alteration and the gap in the message log.

3) Materials/access observed: A dated record in the institutional filing system (index entry, subject line, tracking number); at least three landlord entity records (named accounts, address fields, unit inventories); a coordination channel (creation timestamp, participant list, message thread); an ephemeral messaging medium (channel ID, self-deletion setting, participant accounts); an access log for the filing system (entries for the index alteration); a message-log gap (timestamps with no corresponding stored message); local file-system remnants (deleted channel export, draft message fragments).

4) Indicators & artifacts: Index entry alteration without an accompanying audit ticket; subject-line replacement on a dated record; a message thread containing uniform pricing terms, geographic allotment terms, and penalty terms across competing entity accounts; a migration of the thread from a logged medium to an ephemeral, self-deleting medium; a self-deletion setting enabled on the migrated channel; a contiguous gap in the message log spanning the thread's active period; local artifacts (deleted export file, draft fragments) recovered from disk; an access-log entry showing the index alteration by the actor's named account at a time inconsistent with routine filing.
